steps.why: Axiom 3: space and time are not posited; geometric structure emerges from stable relational configurations. So dimension must be DERIVED from adjacency -- and that discipline is exactly what exposes an imposed clique as an assumption, not a derivation.

The tetrahedron-from-a-clique was geometry imposed. RUNG3-TETRAHEDRON-MINIMUM was retracted for exactly this -- correctly.

steps.expr: Euler (V+F=E+2) + triangular (3F=2E) + uniform degree d (dV=2E) => V = 12/(6-d)
steps.what: the correction: closure alone forces exactly three shells (no clique)
steps.why: REFRAME-CLOSURE-FORCING: with NO clique assumed, the three counting identities of a closed uniform triangular mesh force (d,V) = (3,4) tetrahedron, (4,6) octahedron, (5,12) icosahedron, and d>=6 never closes. The shape IS forced -- machine-checked at maths 4. The three shells are exhibited as explicit meshes, each verified closed with Euler characteristic 2.

steps.expr: separated(v,w) := some third vertex relates differently to each; unseparated count = 0 only for icosa
steps.what: the triad selects the icosahedron: only it has every pair separated by a third
steps.why: SELECTION-BY-RELATIONAL-SEPARATION: a pair of vertices is distinguished only when a THIRD relates differently to each -- rung 2's three-observer condition. Of the three closures, exactly the icosahedron separates every pair (tetra fails all 6 pairs, octa 3 antipodal, icosa 0). d=5 and the TWELVE are forced, not chosen -- and it is the triad doing it.

steps.check: the tetrahedron is a clique of 4 -> 4 equidistant -> dim >= 3
steps.expr: the minimum closure = tetrahedron = 4 mutually adjacent = 4 equidistant => dim >= 3
steps.what: dimension is at least three (the lower bound)
steps.why: the tetrahedron is the only one of the three closures that is a complete graph -- its 4 registrations are MUTUALLY adjacent, hence 4 equidistant points, which force ambient dimension at least three. The adjacency-to-equidistance step is the geometric-balance bridge (a POSTULATE), so the lower bound is derived on top of that stated bridge, not from nothing. THREE-DIMENSIONS-LOWER-BOUND.

steps.check: sphere left ~19.6% uncovered by twelve; D4 admits >=13 neighbours at d=4
steps.expr: sphere not saturated by twelve (3*sqrt3 - 5 uncovered); D4 admits >=13 neighbours at d=4
steps.what: the upper bound is NOT established -- and that is a checked negative, not an absent one
steps.why: the upper bound (dim = 3, not more) was ATTEMPTED via 'twelve fits and no thirteenth fits' and RETRACTED: the substrate's no-thirteenth is TOPOLOGICAL (Euler gives exactly twelve at any d -- a census), never METRIC (a thirteenth could not FIT). Only a metric one bounds the dimension. Two checked facts settle it: (a) SPHERE-IS-NOT-SATURATED-BY-TWELVE -- twelve caps of half-angle pi/6 leave the sphere 3*sqrt3 - 5 ~ 19.6% uncovered (the circle saturates, the sphere frustrates); (b) the D4 root system's 24 roots are pairwise >= 60 degrees, so >=13 fit at d=4. So d=4 is NOT excluded and dim = 3 does NOT follow. dim >= 3 stands; the upper bound does not. Unlike the clique, there is no disconnected repair -- this negative is the answer.
